page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.64-256 is an x86_64 virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9J45 processor architecture. The instance is configured with 64 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. With two threads per core, it exposes 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. It contains no onboard local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for system and runtime data, and it includes no dedicated GPU accelerators.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation emphasizes CPU density over high RAM capacity. This setup maximizes multi-threaded CPU throughput across its 128 vCPUs while avoiding the resource overhead of oversized memory arrays. Qualitatively, this structure provides strong compute efficiency for processing tasks that do not require extensive caching layers. The primary operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning that overall disk throughput and read/write latencies are governed entirely by external block storage attachments.

Because of its core count and dedicated CPU execution, this instance is suited for compute-intensive and parallelized workloads. Appropriate use cases include distributed build and compilation systems, continuous integration pipelines, batch video and data transcoding, computational simulations, and high-throughput stateless web application serving.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.64-256 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 64 physical cores and simultaneous multithreading, the system delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio that optimizes CPU density. The instance has no integrated local storage, requiring remote storage volumes for persistence, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address with zero discrete GPUs. Its lean memory profile relative to core count creates high multi-threaded compute density, making it cost-efficient for pure processing tasks without memory excess. The server is well suited for CPU-bound workloads including distributed software compilation, batch compute jobs, CI/CD runners, parallel simulations, and multi-threaded web backend services.
